div.head: II Cn 26
div.ab: And gesece se æbǽra þeof þæt þæt he gesece, oððe se ðe on hlafordsearwe gemet sig, þæt hig næfre feorh ne gesecean.
And gesece se abere ðeof þæt he gesece, oððe se ðe [on] hlafordsearwe gemet sy, þæt hi næfre feorh ne . . .
Et perquirat abere þeof (fur probatus) quicquid perquirat, aut qui de morte domini sui tractauit, nunquam sibi uitam adquirant.
Be ðeofan. ⁊ gesece se ebǽra ðeof þæt he sece, oððe se ðe on hlafordsearwe gemet sy, þæt hi næfre feorh ne gesecan.
And gesece se æbæra þeof þæt þæt he gesece, oððe se ðe on hlafordsearwe gemet sig, þæt hig næfre feorh ne gesecean.
(Von Dieben. B) Und der offenkundige Dieb oder wer auf Verrath gegen seinen Herrn betroffen ist, mag [von Asylen] aufsuchen was er immer aufsuche: dass sie niemals das Leben [gesichert] erlangen.
(Of thieves. B) And let the manifest thief, or whoever is found guilty of treachery against his lord, seek [sanctuary] wherever he may: they are never to obtain [security of] life.
Concerning thieves. And the proved thief and he who has been discovered in treason against his lord, whatever sanctuary he seeks, shall never be able to save his life.
And anyone convicted of theft or caught conspiring against his lord shall not be able to save his life, no matter where he hides.
div.note: A skips a line (Liebermann supplies ‘on’). Liebermann compares III Eg 7.3.
